explanation: Direct eye contact is expected in Turkish greetings and conversation as a sign of sincerity and engagement, and Turks often hold eye contact during serious discussions. However, devout or conservative individuals may look away from someone of the opposite gender out of modesty, and women may avoid eye contact with unfamiliar men to discourage unwanted attention.
local_tip: Offer natural, direct eye contact when greeting or talking with Turks, but don't force it with someone of the opposite gender who seems to be avoiding it.
regional_note: This modesty-based eye-contact avoidance is most common among devout or conservative Turks and far less of a factor in secular, urban, mixed-gender settings.

also_check.note: Prolonged eye contact can feel confrontational or intimidating; brief glances are preferred.
Direct, sustained eye contact is expected as a sign of honesty and engagement.
Eye contact between men is common, but between men and women it's typically brief or avoided out of modesty.
